
This vignette walks through the Phase 1 macro workflow, the kind of analysis
that feeds an asset allocation committee or a bank ALCO briefing. It uses the
bundled **synthetic** dataset so it runs offline. Pass `source = "fred"` with a
`FRED_API_KEY` set to use real data.

```{r}
library(econkit)
d <- ek_get_series()
head(ek_series_catalog()[, c("id", "title", "transform")])
```

## 1. Recession probability from the yield curve

```{r}
m <- ek_recession_model(d, predictors = "T10Y3M", horizon = 12)
m
p <- predict(m)
plot(p$target_date, p$probability, type = "l", col = "firebrick",
     xlab = "", ylab = "Probability", main = "Recession probability, 12 months ahead")
```

In-sample fit flatters any model. The backtest re-estimates the model at every
forecast origin, using only outcomes that were known at that time. Here it
also allows a 6-month lag before NBER recession dates are announced.

```{r}
bt <- ek_backtest_recession(d, horizon = 12, label_lag = 6)
attr(bt, "metrics")
```

Adding predictors is a one-line change, for example the term spread plus
financial conditions:

```{r}
m2 <- ek_recession_model(d, predictors = c("T10Y3M", "NFCI"), horizon = 12)
rbind(spread = m$metrics, spread_nfci = m2$metrics)
```

## 2. Real-time labour market signal: the Sahm rule

```{r}
d$sahm <- ek_sahm_rule(d$UNRATE)
table(triggered = d$sahm >= 0.5, recession = d$USREC == 1)
```

## 3. Regimes

The growth/inflation quadrant (the "investment clock") is a simple,
transparent regime map for tactical allocation:

```{r}
d$regime <- ek_growth_inflation_regime(
  ek_transform(d$INDPRO, "yoy"),
  ek_transform(d$CPIAUCSL, "yoy")
)
prop.table(table(d$regime))
```

A Markov-switching model gives probabilistic regimes. Use the **filtered**
probabilities for real-time decisions, because smoothed probabilities use
future data.

```{r}
g <- ek_transform(d$INDPRO, "log_diff")[-1]
ms <- ek_markov_switching(g)
ms
plot(d$date[-1], ms$filtered[, "state1"], type = "l", xlab = "",
     ylab = "Probability", main = "Filtered probability of the contraction regime")
```

## 4. Output gap

```{r}
gap <- ek_output_gap(d$INDPRO, method = "hamilton")
plot(d$date, gap$cycle, type = "l", xlab = "", ylab = "% of trend",
     main = "Industrial production gap (Hamilton filter)")
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
```

## 5. Reporting

`ek_render_macro_dashboard("macro-dashboard.html")` renders all of the above
into a self-contained HTML dashboard. The Quarto CLI is required.
